sourceText: We normally use simple present tense to talk about countries and nationalities. Not only the verb to be can be useful to talk about this. Revise the following chart and check some examples.
Even when we talk about this topic, the grammar rules must be respected. To Be – works alone. Other verbs – Use auxiliaries.
MOST COMMON QUESTIONS - Where are you from? - Where do you come from?

To Be verb Other verbs – Auxiliary Introduction John is American Is he American? She comes from England. Does she come from England? They are from Mexico Where are they from? You speak Italian Do you speak Italian? The verb to be is an independent verb it can say a sentence, it can make a question or deny by itself. NO AUXILIARY NEEDED The rest of the verbs are dependent. They use auxiliaries to make questions and to deny an action. Do - I/You/We/They Does - He/She/ It (3rd person singular) *Pronunciation hint: https://youtu.be/EMWmCb1CIdc

sourceText: Functions Examples 1 Talk about oneself and others’ origins. I am from Spain. / She comes from France. 2 State nationalities. He is Dutch. / They are Japanese 3 Talk about the language one speaks. I speak English. / We speak Russian. / You speak Italian.
When we talk about countries and nationalities, there are three main aspects or functions we can cover.
TO CONSIDER All country names, nationalities and languages take CAPITAL LETTERS.

sourceText: It is common to use the simple present tense to talk about routines; also, the use of adverbs of frequency is common on this topic.

ADVERBS OF FREQUENCY 100% Always We always work at night. 90% Usually She is usually late. 80% Normally They normally go to the beach on Saturdays 70% Often I am often at home. 50% Sometimes You sometimes laugh out loud. 30% Occasionally He occasionally cleans his room. 10% Seldom It seldom rains here. 5% Hardly ever Carol hardly ever takes a call. 0% Never John is never on time.

HINT 1. Adverbs go before verbs since they modify them, EXCEPT for To Be. She is always happy 2. NEVER has a negative connotation. (no need for don’t/doesn’t) They never visit me. 3. Adverbs can work in statements, negative sentences and questions.

sourceText: ASPECTS EXAMPLES Talk about general actions everybody makes. She normally has breakfast early. Talk about specific actions each one does. Ruth changes Peter’s clothes twice a day. Talk about activities with specific time of occurrence. Ruth has English class at 6 pm
When we talk about daily routines there are three main aspects that we should take into account using the simple present tense.

The three aspects talk about the same function but they aim different targets in language. The second aspect, as seen in the example, uses mainly general or indefinite time expressions to differentiate itself from the third one.

sourceText: LIKENESS DEGREES EXAMPLES HIGH LEVEL I love drawing cartoons. She is thrilled about learning languages. MEDIUM LEVEL He enjoys working with numbers. They are fans of running marathons. LOW LEVEL We like dancing every weekend. It is fond of hiding bones in the backyard.
We mainly use simple present to express likes and preferences, but there is an interesting fact we need to consider: likeness degrees.
HINT 1. We can also use like and preference expressions to talk about people, food, etc. (Not only for hobbies) 2. The expression thrilled about sometimes is substituted by crazy about.

Statements Questions Negative statements 1. We have a big family Do you have a big family? No, I don’t have a big family. 2. John is my brother Is John your brother? No, John is not my brother. 3. David is my uncle’s son. Is David your uncle’s son? No, he is not my uncle’s son.
Even when we talk about this topic, the grammar rules must be respected. To Be – works alone. Other verbs – use auxiliaries.

sourceText: TO CONSIDER 1. To talk about relationships among family members, we normally use the possessive case (‘s) which denotes belonging and possession and in this case states family relationships. 2. There is more than one scenario for the possessive case: a. Joe’s wife is a doctor. - One owner and one possession. b. Those are my aunt’s (kids). - When the noun was already mentioned and we do not need to state again. c. This is Ted and Mary’s child. - Two owners - One possession. d. These are Jake’s and Jill’s children - Two owners and two possessions. 3. When the noun finishes in ‘s’ we only add the (‘) and the end of the word. E.G. This is James’ child. When this happens, we add an extra syllable in spoken language that is pronounced /әz/. 4. This is not only used to talk about family. E.G. Adrian’s car is blue. 5. When we talk about objects or animals, it is common to use: The legs of the table / The tail of the cat. However, you may find examples using the (‘s).

sourceText: Aspects Examples 1 Describe general things about family. My family is big. / Our family has good traditions. 2 State relationships. Peter is my brother. / Kevin and Tom are my dad’s nephews. / I have a step mother. 3 Talk about family members. John is my cousin, he is a doctor and he works in a hospital.
When we talk about families and relatives there are certain aspects that we can include in this topic.
TO CONSIDER Most of the statements about family take To Be. However, we can use other verbs to talk about this matter.

nextRows.title: Khai’s Family My name is Khai and I am from China. I am 26 years old. I have a big family. My parents have six children, three sons and three daughters. My siblings and I live with them. I am the oldest. My sister Shinmei is the second one. She is a science teacher at university and she is 24 years old. Our brothers’ names are Tenkei and Senku and our sisters’ names are Megumi and Kumiko. My father is an only child so, we have no relatives on my father’s side. On my mother’s side, we have two uncles, three aunts and eleven cousins. See? We are a big family.

sourceText: It is common to use the simple present tense to talk about jobs and occupations as we saw on the useful language before.

To Be verb Other verbs – Auxiliary Introduction John is a doctor Is he a doctor? John makes shoes. What does John do? They are bakers What is their job? I work as a store manager. What do you do for a living? The verb to be is an independent verb it can say a sentence, it can make a question or deny by itself. NO AUXILIARY NEEDED The rest of the verbs are dependent. They use auxiliaries to make questions and to deny an action. Do - I/You/We/They Does - He/She/ It (3rd person singular) *Remember pronunciation tip from unit 2.
In the following chart you will see how this structure can be implemented.
Examples: Jake works in a bank. Does he work in a bank? I don’t work as a waiter / Do you work as a waiter?

sourceText: We normally use simple present tense to talk about food. Check out the following examples.

STATEMENTS QUESTIONS NEGATIVE STATEMENTS 1. There is one apple on the table. Is there one apple on the table? There isn’t an apple on the table. 2. There are a lot of eggs in the basket. Are there a lot of eggs in the basket? There aren’t any of eggs in the basket. 3. I have some water in the bottle. Do you have any water in the bottle? I don’t have any water in the bottle. To consider: 1. We use the expressions There is (singular) / there are (plural) to say something exists. 2. We can use other verbs to talk about food. See example number 3. 3. When we talk about food, we need to talk about quantity. We use containers and quantifiers: Some – Any – a lot of – Few / A few - None – lots of – Much - Many. Also, there are two main questions when we talk about quantities: How much – Used for uncountable nouns. How much milk is there left? How many – Used for countable nouns. How many do you have?

nextRows.title: TO CONSIDER - This / that (singular) These / Those (plural) are demonstratives we use to talk about possessions. This / These (close objects) – That / Those (far objects) - Whose: wh word used to ask for possessions: Whose USB is this? - Possessive adjectives can also be used to talk about belongings: This is my house. - Every possessive adjective has a possessive pronoun: My / Mine, Your / yours, His / His, Her / Hers, Its / Its, Our / Ours, Their / Theirs (used when we already know what we are talking about) - Demonstrative pronouns can also work as adjectives. E.G That house is blue. Let’s watch the video on the platform.

We normally use simple present tense to talk about belongings. Check out the following examples.

Statements Questions Negative Statements 1. This is Joe’s car. Is this Joe’s car? / Whose car is this? This is not Joe’s car. 2. That is our house. Is that your house? / Whose house is that? That is not ours. 3. These are my keys. Are these your keys? / Whose keys are these? These are not mine. 4. Those are Mary’s children. Are those Mary’s children? / Whose Children are those? No, those aren’t Mary’s.

nextRows.title: We normally use simple present tense to talk about places and where they are.

sourceText: We normally use simple present tense to talk about places and where they are.

Statements Questions Negative statements 1. The park is on the Main Avenue. IS the park on the Main Avenue? / Where is the park? The park is not on the Main Avenue. 2. The public library is in front of the bank; so, take the train downtown. How do I get to the public library? I am not sure, Do you know where is it? 3. To get to the Caffe, go along the park. Do you have to go across the park to get to the Caffe? You don’t have to go between the park and local market to get to the Caffe. 4. The restaurant is opposite to the bakery. Where is the restaurant? The restaurant is not next to the bakery; it is opposite.
TO CONSIDER - Prepositions are used to indicate location. - Downtown does not use any preposition: I am going downtown. - More than 1 verb can be used to talk about directions. / Questions vary too.

sourceText: Aspects Examples 1 Ask for directions. Where is the park? / How do I get to the bank? / Is the Caffe across the street? 2 State where a place is. I think the public library is along the main avenue on Jefferson Street’s corner. 3 Explain how to get to a place. You have to take the number 10 bus, get off at the West park, walk 1 block and you find the bank.
When we talk about places, we can consider the following aspects.
TO CONSIDER Prepositions are essential to work with these 3 aspects since they state locations and placement.

nextRows.title: We normally talk about places and we include the use of adjectives to describe their characteristics. Adjectives are words we use to denote specificities about people, places or situations.

sourceText: We normally talk about places and we include the use of adjectives to describe their characteristics. Adjectives are words we use to denote specificities about people, places or situations.

Statements Questions Negative statements 1. Mexico has the ancient ruins of the Mayas Does Mexico have the ancient ruins of the Mayas? No, it does not have the ancient ruins. 2. Santa Elena is a small, beautiful and hot town in the South of Venezuela. How is Santa Elena? It is not big or cold. 3. We live in a tiny and cozy town near the borders. Where do you live? I live in a tiny and cozy town but it is not quite.

TO CONSIDER 1. Adjectives come before the object, place or people they describe. 2. They can also be after one verb: My house is beautiful (mainly after To Be). 3. Adjectives do not change because of gender. E.G: She is beautiful / The park is beautiful. 4. Adjectives are not pluralized. E.G: They are talls.❌ They are tall. ✅

Santa Elena is a small, beautiful and hot town in the South of Venezuela. How is Santa Elena? It is not big or cold. 3. We live in a tiny and cozy town near the borders. Where do you live? I live in a tiny and cozy town but it is not quite.

TO CONSIDER 1. Adjectives come before the object, place or people they describe. 2. They can also be after one verb: My house is beautiful (mainly after To Be). 3. Adjectives do not change because of gender. E.G: She is beautiful / The park is beautiful. 4. Adjectives are not pluralized. E.G: They are talls.❌ They are tall. ✅

sourceText: Descriptive Functions Examples 1 Give an opinion -This is a beautiful city. - It is not. It is crowded and noisy. 2 State size They have a big house. 3 Describe shape We need a round table. 4 State age We live in an old building. 5 Define color The sky is blue today! 6 Determine origin It is a German dog. 7 State material Please, buy some plastic cups. 8 State purpose He has a sports car.
Adjectives can be used in any tense: present, past, future. They are mainly used to describe different characteristics. Check the following examples.

TO CONSIDER More than one adjective can be used to describe one single thing. It has to respect the order presented in the characteristics. E.G. They have a gorgeous, big, new, American, wooden, beach house. *not always all the characteristics are used*

It has an ancient square named Er and there are some medieval walls as part of our history. It is a tranquil place to live and to visit.

Visit this country if you have the chance.

nextRows.title: TO CONSIDER 1. Adjectives can be divided into two groups: / Short (1 or 2 syllables) / Long (2 or more syllables). 2. Short adjectives take the –er + than particles: Joe is taller than Jim. 3.Long adjectives take the more + than particles: It is more expensive here than there. 4.Short adjectives that finish in –y change to I + er: She is prettier than you. 5. There are irregular adjectives: Good – Better than / Bad – Worse than. 6. We use the particles ‘as / as’ to state similarities: Joe is as tall as Jake. 7. There are adjectives who do not receive comparison degrees; those adjective have absolute meaning: This is the final test / Those people are dead. 8. nextRows.title: TO CONSIDER 1. Adjectives are divided into two groups: / Short (1 or 2 syllables) / Long (2 or more syllables). 2. Short adjectives take the –est particles: Joe is the tallest in his family. 3. Long adjectives take the most particle: It is the most expensive restaurant in the city. 4. Short adjectives that finish in –y change to I + est: She is the prettiest at school. 5. There are irregular adjectives: Good – Better than – The Best / Bad – Worse than – The Worst. 6. The superlative for less than is: The least. E.G: That is the least of my worries. 7. ABSOLUTE adjectives do not take superlative level

Short adjectives that finish in –y change to I + est: She is the prettiest at school. 5. There are irregular adjectives: Good – Better than – The Best / Bad – Worse than – The Worst. 6. The superlative for less than is: The least. E.G: That is the least of my worries. 7. ABSOLUTE adjectives do not take superlative level

My Best Friend My best friend, Cloe, lives in the most wonderful city of all times. She lives in Seoul where the greatest technological advances occur every day. She studies in one of the biggest designing institute of the city and it has the best reputation of the local people. I want to visit her, but right now I have the worst economic situation ever. However, she has the most amazing job too, so she wants to pay for my plane ticket, I am so excited!

1. Who is her best friend? 2. Where does she live? 3. Which is the most wonderful city of all times? 4. When do the greatest technological advances occur there? 5. data.transcript: It was the longest plane trip I have ever taken. It wasn't that long and you enjoyed it at least. Yes man it was the longest but the best trip of my entire life so far. Tokyo is one of the biggest city in the world with the most charming places to visit. Indeed but one of the most expensive too. However what do you like most about Tokyo? Well I think the best place to visit is the Tokyo Tower. You can see the entire city from there. You can have one of the best meals in the city and it was the cheapest place. No way how about the Shugun Castle? It is the most amazing place to go. It has a lot of history in it. Hmm still I don't have a Tokyo Tower.

sourceText: Ongoing actions are stated through the present progressive. Check out the following examples.

Statements Questions Negative statements 1. I am doing my homework now. Are you doing your homework now? I am not doing my homework now. 2. They are talking on the phone right now. Are they talking on the phone right now? They are not talking on the phone right now. 3. He is practicing for the soccer finale these days. Is he practicing for the soccer finale these days? He is not practicing for the soccer finale these days. 4. Currently, They are rebuilding the house. Are they currently rebuilding the house? No, they are not currently rebuilding the house.
TO CONSIDER 1. Verb To Be acts as an auxiliary. 2. -Ing form is added to end of the main verbs. 3. Do/Does are not used here.

sourceText: Functions Examples 1 Ongoing actions. He is taking a shower now. / We are having English class at the moment. 2 Actions happening for a certain time period. We are rehearsing for the recital these days. / For now, I am doing work from home. 3 Actions happening once and again. Jake is always eating burgers. / They are always playing soccer.
When we use the present progressive we can take into account some functions.
TO CONSIDER Time phrases may vary a little depending on the function we want to express. There is a fourth function related to expressing future.

Vacations Dear Annie, how are you? I am writing these lines from the hotel room. I am having a good time these days because Cancun is so beautiful. We are getting ready now because we are going on a tour in some minutes. My brother is enjoying every moment and my dad is making all he can to make us happy. Right now, we are also having breakfast. How are your vacations going? Please write. Love, Laurie.

1. Annie is writing the email. (T) (F) 2. She is writing from the hotel restaurant. (T) (F) 3. She is having a good time. (T) (F) 4. They are getting ready now. (T) (F) 5. They are not going on a tour. (T) (F) 6. Her brother is enjoying every moment. (T) (F) 7. Her father is making all he can to make them happy. (T) (F) 8. They are having breakfast now. (T) (F)

data.transcript: Is it raining? No, it looks like, but it's not raining right now. However, it is raining all these days. Okay, so it's cloudy now. Can you let me know if it starts raining? Well, I'm correcting some exams. And making lunch at the moment. So I cannot promise anything. Hey, I'm making lunch this week, remember? Don't worry. Oh right, and I'm doing laundry this week. So I'll let you know if it rains. Perfect, thanks. Wait, why do you want to know if it rains? Oh, I like running under the rain.

nextRows.title: What a place! Two years ago, we visited one of the most amazing places of the world. We went to Japan. We arrived to Tokyo and we stayed there for 3 days. After that, we traveled by train to Odaiba; the trip was marvelous and it was super fast. When we arrived there, we looked for a hotel and we decided to stay in a typical Japanese inn that we found downtown. We tried the traditional Ramen and the original sushi, IT WAS AMAZING! After 3 days, we took another train and went to Hikarigaoka; We visited my dad’s friend there and after two days, we flew back home. This was one of the best trips in my life.

sourceText: Talking about habits in the past leads us to use simple past tense structure; though, it is necessary to work with used to.

TO CONSIDER 1. Used to is a fixed expression that comes before a verb in simple form. 2. If the sentence has the auxiliary DID, used to goes in simple form. 3. Other useful expressions: but not anymore / Back in my childhood / When I was a child / When I was younger etc. 4. Used to can be used in simple present tense to talk about customs people have. E.G. She is used to read the newspaper in the mornings.

Used to John used to attend dancing classes all nights. Did John use to attend dancing classes all nights? I used to make cakes back in my school days. Did you use to make cakes back in your school day?

nextRows.title: Memories! I always remember my childhood. I used to spend hours with my friends nearby the river swimming, playing and sometimes camping. We used to go there almost every Saturday to play at the tree house and to listen to good music. I have to admit that we used to be very noisy kids; however, we used to be good kids and we never made anything terrible…well, we used to ring doorbells to our neighbors so we were not angels either. I’d wish those times to be back, kids now do not enjoy life since technology has overtaken them; I truly think we had the greatest childhood.

nextRows.title: When we talk about actions happening in the past, we need to use the past progressive tense.

sourceText: When we talk about actions happening in the past, we need to use the past progressive tense.

TO CONSIDER 1. We use the verb to be as auxiliary. In both forms: was / were. 2. The main verb takes the –ing form as seen in the examples. 3. When is used to connect two ideas; in this case it presents an action that interrupts another one. 4. While is used to state two actions happening simultaneously. 5. Negative forms are wasn’t / weren’t.

Past Progressive tense I was eating when the earthquake started. Were you eating when the earthquake started? They were relaxing at the beach when they gave the tsunami alert. Were they relaxing at the beach when they gave the tsunami alert? He was running fast while the tornado was chasing him. Was he running fast while the tornado was chasing him?

data.transcript: Tell us Mr. Robinson, how did it all start? We were at the ski lodge having lunch when suddenly we heard a loud noise. And then what happened? Were there others having lunch too? No, only me. And the owners of course. They were cooking while I was waiting for my lunch and then it all started. You mean the avalanche? Can you give us some more details? As I said, we heard a loud noise when then the things were trembling and we saw it. What do you see? A huge white snow wall approaching. Thank god the owner had hatched to a subterranean bunker so we could save ourselves. Well, what an experience. Thank you for your time Mr. Robinson. No, thank you. Am I famous now? Well dear audience, thank you for watching. Davey, back to you in the studio.

nextRows.title: Survivors! 2 years ago, my family and I went to Thailand for spending our holidays. We were having a good time and the city was giving us all what we expected. When we arrived, we were having problems to find the hotel, but a woman helped us and we got safe. The days were passing by while we were having the greatest time of our lives; we had the chance to try traditional food when we were visiting local markets. On the fifth day, we were having a great time at the beach when suddenly an alarm sounded…it was announcing that a tsunami was approaching. Everybody was running while we were trying to stay together in the middle of the terrible moment. Some minutes later, a big wave crashed over the land and lots of water was running over people while they were trying to escape… fortunately, we could get to high hill and survived.

When we arrived, we were having problems to find the hotel, but a woman helped us and we got safe. The days were passing by while we were having the greatest time of our lives; we had the chance to try traditional food when we were visiting local markets. On the fifth day, we were having a great time at the beach when suddenly an alarm sounded…it was announcing that a tsunami was approaching. Everybody was running while we were trying to stay together in the middle of the terrible moment. Some minutes later, a big wave crashed over the land and lots of water was running over people while they were trying to escape… fortunately, we could get to high hill and survived.

Well, that too. Hey, how about VR developer? Joe’s brother is going to start working at a VR company as a developer. Amazing! When is he going to start working there? I guess on July, but I am going to ask Joe to confirm. Do you think he is going to get free demos to try? I hope he does! So maybe, we are going to be able to play with Joe. OMG! If that is true, we are going to be the luckiest kids on the block. Totally! I am going to ask Joe now. Let’s go!

sourceText: When we talk about weather we do not only use simple present. We can also use will. Check the following examples.
TO CONSIDER 1. Will is used to state future. 2. Verbs go in simple form after using will. 3. Future Time phrases are also needed. 4. Adverbs also help to state meaning.

Will – Future It will rain soon. It is cloudy. Will it rain soon? It is cold; it will probably snow later. Will it probably snow later? Go fresh, it will be sunny at the beach. Will it be sunny at the beach?

Well, you must dress the parents once you are there and tell them how honoured you are for the invitation. Do I have to smile all night? No, there will be hypocrisy, but you need to look happy and you must not ask for more food. What if I'm hungry? You should wait for them to tell you and you should not look hungry, okay? Okay, I will do my best. And you should not be bossy. You are my friend. I'm not bossy. I have a talent for leading people.

An insight I always talk to myself, I find it interesting and refreshing. I know I should talk to other people for advise or just to share some of the things or situations I live, but it is very difficult. People have to be trustworthy and they need to prove themselves friend. “I should not look back into other bad experiences” I say to myself all the time; however, I must be clear too and I can’t be friends with everyone at first. People must give back what they receive and they should act towards others the same way others act towards them, but I guess not everyone thinks like me.

Main verbs must be in past participle. 6. There is a progressive tense that can be used here. E.G I have been waiting for the bus for two hours

nextRows.title: We can use present perfect tense to communicate different functions. Check out the following examples.

sourceText: We can use present perfect tense to communicate different functions. Check out the following examples.

Functions Examples 1 Express actions that started in the past and still continue. They have visited us for two weeks already. You have been tall since you were a child. 2 Talk about actions than happened only once or certain times. He has just been there once. We have stayed at your place many times. 3 State unfinished actions We have been expecting him to change for so long. 4 Point out finished actions -Why are you so tired? -I’ve been getting ready for the test all week.

Such a great life! John is 25 years old. In such a young life, he has known many places. He has been in Europe for the last two weeks; he has gone sightseeing every day and he has already visited many places. Today, he has not gone out of the hotel yet, but he has just had breakfast so he is getting ready to go out. He has been to other places in his life and he has seen and stayed in a range of inns, boarding houses, lodges etc. around the world. He’s living his life the way he has planned and so far, he has gotten and achieved all what he wanted. This trip will finish the upcoming Friday, but he is already planning what to do for the upcoming holidays.

data.transcript: Joe, tell us, what does it feel like to be an exchange student? Well, Mr. Freeman, it has been an amazing experience for me to be part of this program. What have you acquired during these two years of scholarship? I must say I have obtained professional and personal skills. How's that? Well, I used to be very shy, but meeting new people and having visited new places and sightseeing, changed my perception completely. Is that so? How about the program itself? Magnificent. I have nothing but good references from all my professors and the institution. Would you like to try another program some other time? I have already applied for one, haven't I? They have not sent the applications yet, but for sure we'll look into yours.

My dad wanted all of us there. What for? Did someone come to visit? Yep. Grandma came along with someone else. Someone else? Somebody has a younger boyfriend than her now. No way. He hasn't yet.

sourceText: People Places Things All Everybody Everyone Everywhere Everything Positive Somebody Someone Somewhere Something Negative Anybody Anyone Anywhere Anything None Nobody No one Nowhere Nothing
We use indefinite pronouns to make generalizations about people, places and things.

To Consider 1. All indefinite pronouns have a definite connotation when using them. 2. The ones using “Any” mainly work in questions or negative sentences. However, it is possible to see them in positive sentences. 3. The ones using the particle “No” have already a full negative connotation like “never”. 4. They are used with verbs in singular (i.e. the verb for the 3rd person singular)

sourceText: We may consider the relative clauses or pronouns as details we want or have to add to the information we already know. There are possible scenarios we can check out.
Scenarios Examples 1 Emphasis I don’t know why she didn’t come to the party. 2 Vague References My uncle was in the hospital where your aunt was operated.

To consider These are not the only possible scenarios. Check out the following sentences: I know someone who would love to see you! Remember what I told you. *How can also be used here: I want to know how you did this (working as complement) She did amazing, how she normally does, that night at the concert.(emphatic information)
All clauses can work like this

nextRows.title: To Consider 1. Adjectives that finish in -ING are normally used to describe situations or things. 2. Adjectives that finish in -ED are used to describe how people feel because of something. 3. Adjectives may be unique or classified into a pattern. E.G.: Glib / Silly / Tiny 4. Some -ING adjectives are used to describe people if they are producing something in someone else: I am annoyed, you know? Joey is so annoying, always talking too much. 5. Another issue is that some adjectives ending -IC and -ICAL tend to be confusing; here is a list for patterns https://www.thefreedictionary.com/Commonly-Confused-Suffixes-ic-vs-ical.htm#:~:text=The%20suffixes%20%E2%80%9C%2Dic%E2%80%9D%20and,are%20notoriously%20difficult%20to%20distinguish.

Some -ING adjectives are used to describe people if they are producing something in someone else: I am annoyed, you know? Joey is so annoying, always talking too much. 5. Another issue is that some adjectives ending -IC and -ICAL tend to be confusing; here is a list for patterns https://www.thefreedictionary.com/Commonly-Confused-Suffixes-ic-vs-ical.htm#:~:text=The%20suffixes%20%E2%80%9C%2Dic%E2%80%9D%20and,are%20notoriously%20difficult%20to%20distinguish.

nextRows.title: Conditionals link two different clauses as we learned in the last unit. First conditional links an action or circumstance in the present with another one in the future.

sourceText: Conditionals link two different clauses as we learned in the last unit. First conditional links an action or circumstance in the present with another one in the future.

DEFINITIONS & POSSIBLE CASE INDEPENDENT CLAUSE DEPENDENT CLAUSE 1 They can exist alone You’ll get a sunburn (IF you get too much sun.) 2 They need another clause to exist (He will need an MRI) IF he hits his head. 3 Switching Clauses If she cuts herself while cooking , She’ll probably need stitches. To Consider 1. The use of will is necessary since it is the way consequences in the future are expressed. 2. Sometimes, ‘can’ is also used to state a consequence. E.G: If you get wet under the rain, you can get a cold. 3. When the IF clause is the first one, it needs to be separated by a comma (,) from the other clause.

nextRows.title: We can use the first conditional aiming the following functions or aspects

sourceText: We can use the first conditional aiming the following functions or aspects

Functions Examples 1 Talk about illnesses and conditions people can get I will have to see a doctor if the fever continues. If they do not operate him, he will lose his leg. 2 Warn people If Shane does not pass the course, he will be grounded for months. The boys will not go to the party if they do not clean their room.

To consider These two areas are not the only ones that can be covered. Generally, talking about consequences may include the use of the conditional. Should is also used sometimes to substitute IF. E.G: Should he fail, we will lose the game.

data.transcript: Joe move! If we get early to the hospital we'll be back home in the afternoon. Come on dad, can I escape today? Are you out of your mind? You won't recover if you do not get to therapy as a doctor said. What will happen if I do not go just one day? Dear Lord Joe, you will deal with the fact of going to therapy if you want to go back to normal. Breaking your leg while skating was nobody's fault but yours. Face it! If my leg heals well, will I go back to skate? This is unbelievable. I told you, no more skating. You will get better and you'll go to college this year if there is still a chance. Fine dad, fine! Hey, can we give Teddy a lift to the hospital? He needs to get his father's MRI results. Tell him to be ready if he wants the ride. How is his father, by the way? He's doing better, though the hemorrhagic stroke was some game. I bet it was. Well, move, we're already late.

Authored audio transcript:
Joe move! If we get early to the hospital we'll be back home in the afternoon. Come on dad, can I escape today? Are you out of your mind? You won't recover if you do not get to therapy as a doctor said. What will happen if I do not go just one day? Dear Lord Joe, you will deal with the fact of going to therapy if you want to go back to normal. Breaking your leg while skating was nobody's fault but yours. Face it! If my leg heals well, will I go back to skate? This is unbelievable. I told you, no more skating. You will get better and you'll go to college this year if there is still a chance. Fine dad, fine! Hey, can we give Teddy a lift to the hospital? He needs to get his father's MRI results. Tell him to be ready if he wants the ride. How is his father, by the way? He's doing better, though the hemorrhagic stroke was some game. I bet it was. Well, move, we're already late.

To Consider 1. The use of would/could is commonly seen here to express the possibility about something. 2. The dependent clauses are used in simple past tense. 3. When the IF clause is the first one, it needs to be separated by a comma (,) from the other clause. 4. For the verb BE, the correct form to use is: If I were...

sourceText: We can use the first conditional aiming the following functions or aspects
To consider Second Conditional can also be used to give advice to people. E.G: If I were you, I would not do that.

Functions Examples 1 Considering life decisions If I were a doctor, I would be a plastic surgeon. She would definitely choose Mike if she ever got married. 2 Being in someone else’s shoes I would say yes if I were her. If he were a professional, they would probably hire him.
data.sourceTitle: We can use the first conditional aiming the following functions or aspects
nativeParagraphs: We can use the first conditional aiming the following functions or aspects
Second Conditional can also be used to give advice to people. E.G:
If I were you, I would not do that.
If I were a doctor, I would be a plastic surgeon.

How to be in life I am sure there are many conceptions on how to proceed in life regarding many issues. Fairly speaking, I believe people need to be honest to get along with others. Additionally, by respecting others, you can get to be respected as well. People have to understand that respect and honesty are fundamental to have and keep healthy relationships in life. I have decided to live by these standards and it would be a great idea for people to consider them, and have the courage to admit not having used these values in certain circumstances, in order to say they’re sorry, and mend what they did. What do you think of this? Do you agree?

data.transcript: My best friend can't understand it when the kids go crazy around the house. I honestly understand her Kids are full of energy, but I love it when they can't play without making a big mess. I Really don't mind it when they play quietly and even I like it when they want me to play with them But sometimes they do not understand when to stop. There are some other phrases that may be considered adverbial clauses as well. Condition: if / Unless / As if / Only if - You’ll get permission only if your father agrees. Place: Everywhere / Wherever / Anywhere - Wherever I go, I see her. Reason: Now that / Because / Since - You can start painting the room now that your brother is gone.

sourceText: The most common modal to work with requests is would. However, there are other uses and modals that we can include here.

MODALS TO USE STATEMENTS NOTES 1 WOULD I would like a cheese cake. Used to express wishes 2 WOULD in questions Would you pass me the salt? Please. Used to express requests 3 WOULD + Prefer She’d prefer to have a cold drink Used to express preferences To Consider 1. Would can also be used for offers. E.G. Would you like a cup of tea? 2. Can is also a modal that may be used for informal requests. E.G. Can I go to the bathroom? 3. Using will at the end of a sentence also implies a request. E.G. Stop bothering your sister, will you? 4. May is also used for formal requests. E.G. May I say something?

nextRows.title: We can use would to express different ideas.

sourceText: We can use would to express different ideas.

Functions Examples 1 Expressing requests Would you call Annie and tell her about the meeting? 2 Making offers Would you like ice tea or hot coffee? 3 Establishing preferences They’d prefer to stay home tonight. 4 Wishing I’d love to get that scholarship.

To consider Would also works with the adverbial particle rather. Generally, it is used to state you choose something / someone over another one. E.G: I’d rather take the red one, thanks. What would you rather do?

Normally people are supposed to open it so the person can see his face. However, it is not a custom to do it, but it is very common. I understand. In some cultures, it is not acceptable to open the presents in front of others. Yeah, I guess every place has its own ways. Hey, how about being invited to dinner? Well, in Canada, people are very strict with time. If someone invites you to have a meal, the custom is for the guests to arrive on time. Not early, not late. Wow, that's something really difficult for a Latin person. Really? You guys never get on time? It's very unlikely. You are not supposed to arrive late, but we always do. And when you arrive on time, the host is not ready. Unbelievable.

data.transcript: As you all know, we Venezuelans are happy people. We always have a smile, even for those we need for the first time. Also, it is a custom that if you have a friend for a long time, that guy will for sure be your kid's handle. Additionally, people in my country are supposed to practice hospitality, and if you visit a home, you are expected to be hungry and eat a lot. Furthermore, it is completely okay to laugh out loud in your inner circle. Though we're not supposed to disrupt other's peace. Finally, I can say that it is super normal to say goodbye like four different times in different places of the house after a family meeting or a party has taken place, even when you are already in the car. Yup, that is a little bit of us.

Additionally, people in my country are supposed to practice hospitality, and if you visit a home, you are expected to be hungry and eat a lot. Furthermore, it is completely okay to laugh out loud in your inner circle. Though we're not supposed to disrupt other's peace. Finally, I can say that it is super normal to say goodbye like four different times in different places of the house after a family meeting or a party has taken place, even when you are already in the car. Yup, that is a little bit of us.

nextRows.title: I wasn’t prepared for the culture shock of being an international student For any student, moving away from home can be daunting. But I didn’t expect student life in Scotland to be all that different from my home of the Netherlands. After all, we get the same news and TV shows online. However, when I moved from Amsterdam to study at the University of Stirling, I began to realise that a few small things were catching me off balance. I was suffering a minor cultural shock. In my first year, I quickly found out my English was not as good as I had assumed. Most of my flatmates were born and raised in Scotland, and I constantly found myself having to ask people to repeat themselves. Their Scottish accents didn’t help and I was mispronouncing names and places all the time. I also got confused about small cultural things. Much to my flatmates’ amusement, it took me two Christmases to figure out that mince pies are not actually filled with minced beef. The language barrier meant that public transport was tricky at first. I found the lack of information about bus prices and how and where to get tickets really surprising. It turned a simple 15-minute journey into a daunting task. Article retrieved from: https://www.theguardian.com/education/2016/mar/30/i-wasnt-prepared-for-the-culture-shock-of-being-an-international-student

nextRows.title: How have women’s legal rights evolved over the last 50 years? Today, women have just three-quarters of the legal rights of men. In 1970, it was less than half. The Women, Business and the Law 2020 report presented results from our recent effort to document how laws have changed since 1970. This exceptional dataset has already facilitated ground-breaking research that shows that a country’s performance on the Women, Business and the Law index is associated with more women in the labor force, a smaller wage gap between men and women, and greater investments in health and education. We hope that sharing the data and reform descriptions on our website will lead to more evidence that will inspire policymakers to change their laws so that more women can contribute to economic growth and development. Analysis of 1,518 reforms across 50 years and 190 economies yields some interesting insights. First of all, significant progress has been made around the world. Second, the pace of reform has varied across regions. The high-income OECD and Sub-Saharan Africa regions have noted the biggest progress both in terms of volume of reforms and improvement in their average WBL index scores. The third interesting finding is that progress has been uneven across the eight different areas of the law measured by Women, Business and the Law. Most reforms were recorded in the areas of workplace protections and laws dealing with working parents. Despite the progress that has been made, more work remains. Article retrieved from : https://blogs.worldbank.org/opendata/how-have-womens-legal-rights-evolved-over-last-50-years

Most reforms were recorded in the areas of workplace protections and laws dealing with working parents. Despite the progress that has been made, more work remains. nextRows.title: People Can Change, But That Doesn't Mean They Will Most people agree: Everyone makes mistakes. You might use this phrase to console a loved one who’s done something they regret or boost self-compassion when you mess up yourself. Perhaps you add the reassurance, “You’ll do better next time,” or vow to use your experience to improve in the future. These common sayings imply people can change — and they absolutely can. Anyone can make an effort to alter specific habits or behaviors. Even some aspects of attitude and personality can change over time… with some dedicated effort. Yet while people can change, not everyone does. How can you tell if someone will ever really address certain behaviors? What factors make improvement more likely? Keep reading to find out. Change is often complicated, and it doesn’t always happen the way you envision. The following reminders can help you maintain a realistic perspective about the process. Article retrieved from: https://www.healthline.com/health/do-people-change

sourceText: Let’s take a look how we may express ideas or suggestions.

Functions Examples 1 State a more appealing option They’d better not take those samples until they are ready. 2 Come up with ideas Children can share the magazines in small teams to finish faster, don’t you think? 3 Reflect on a thought Shouldn’t we look into it before making a choice? To consider 1. The use of had better, can and should is not fixed to the functions of the examples. 2. Given the context, each of them can work with any of the functions. 3. Should can be used as an alternative to if. E.G: Should you need internet, the code is in this card.

data.transcript: Josh here, what's up Dylan? Hey man, how's it going? Listen, I'm calling in regards to the appointment we have on Saturday. The one with the Mr. Fujidaka? What about it? Everything has been set for the lunch. What if everything hasn't? Wait, what? Why that call and reservation did not go through? We'd better think of something to solve this without getting him upset. If we don't close the deal, we're gonna start looking for some other job Dylan. Don't you think I know that? Maybe if we invited him to a very expensive Japanese restaurant, he would feel flatter and admit the fact of us switching places at last minute. We still have two days to go, we can have Laila call him, and she should offer him the chance of that traditional meal. Should he succeed? We're going to get a raise. Well, we'd better get the plan in motion and get back on that horse. I'll call Laila and we'll have all the pumps on deck.

nextRows.title: Successful Managers Know That Luck Goes With Effort Experienced managers learn that success is a combination of luck and effort. Arrogant and inexperienced managers may think any success is entirely from effort. They’d better change that idea. Anyone who works in management long enough will see many managers rise and fall according to their measures of luck and effort. Some of the managers who fall end up rising again through ambition and perseverance while others do not. Firings, demotions, layoffs and personal problems derail many careers. The ones who bounce back, lick their wounds and find a way to rise once more so they can superpass whatever makes them fall. The most successful managers have exceptional traits including higher than average intelligence, character, ambition, energy and leadership skills. But luck does play a part. Even they can’t control everything or guarantee success in any and all situations; shouldn’t this be something to think of? For example, a senior manager who took over a struggling operation couldn’t do anything about a key subordinate who sadly was dying of leukemia. Nor could he do anything about other underperforming business units that were dragging down the entire division, which ultimately led to its demise. Article retrieved and adapted from: https://medium.com/leading-and-managing/successful-managers-know-that-luck-goes-with-effort-d4cf6bc439a2

data.transcript: Hey Sean, what do you really expect to have in 10 years from now? Well, I had thought it was to be a super rich man, but lately I have decided to have a family and a home. Wow, so you don't want the money now? For sure I want it, but I also need someone to spend the rest of my life with. And the idea of having a family kills me so badly. Having a family, not my golf team man, but good for you. For me, rather than having a family, I'd love to get the best job. In fact, my own company so I can get to be the business man I have always wanted to be, rich and famous. A business man cloaked in silk and drowned in money? What else could a 30 year old man decide to have? Right up my alley Sean, maybe forming a family can be a fulfilled desire after that.

Have you gotten it yet? One of the most difficult decisions in life is choosing who will accompany you for the rest of it. A lot of people dream of having the ideal match for life and striving through many experiences, they may get it. Most of us would love to share our life with someone kind, honest and respectful, being these some of the good qualities we can mention. Getting very ugly, situations can get the worst from us, so it is natural that we expect to have a person who makes us come to our senses when necessary. However, happiness does not depend on having someone and we have to be clear on that. A happy life, you can create it on your own.

sourceText: B. Listen to the audio and answer the questions your teacher makes.

Do it yourself It is very common to listen to people say: If you want to do something, do it yourself. Have others make chores or favors for or to you does not always end well. Get people to work or do things the way you want has always been kind of a challenge. If we refer to a professional area, you need to have people trained so they know what you want and expect. On a more personal level, getting others to know you, and getting to know them will make things easier in dealing with different situations that may occur. Whatever it is, professional or personal, having others do things for us, or getting things done by others is something challenging.

KEEP THE CHIN UP To be stalwart and courageous in a tough situation. Don't let the difficulties intimidate you; keep your chin up. WALK OUT ON To suddenly leave a job, a relationship or other situation. Everyone was shocked when he walked out on his wife of fourteen years. COME OUT SWINGING To be confrontational. He came out swinging at his critics, accusing them of having their own agenda. BEEF UP To become big and muscular. We need to find some new players to beef up the team. TURN ASIDE To refuse entry to somewhere. His job application was turned aside when they saw his criminal record. TIDE OVER Temporary help (often financial) Have another piece of cake. It'll tide you over till supper. CRACK UP Go through an emotional breakdown. The entire group cracked up at the joke of their teacher.

E.G. We need to call it off. 5. Separable phrasal verbs work also together. E.G. We called off the meeting.

Knock it off! Have you ever met someone who is so annoying that you can not stand him? I think we all have. Coming across with such a character and having him around may make us shout at some point ‘hey man, knock it off! However, being in peace with everyone is something we all must go for. We need to bear in mind that each person is different so that brings up different situations to deal with. Nevertheless, neither disrespect nor abuse should be born from anyone, so we need to set limits and boundaries.

HAVE A BONE TO PICK An unpleasant issue or grievance that need discussion. I have a bone to pick with you about that email. GO FOR BROKE To risk everything and go for an all out effort. If you decide to go for broke, you can’t be thinking about what will happen if you fail. MAKE A CLEAN SWEEP To remove all unwanted people or things in order to start afresh. The new leaders wanted to make a clean sweep of the discredited old order GIVE THE NOD To show one's approval of someone or something. I gave Amanda the nod because she is the most qualified candidate. HAVE AN AXE TO GRIND To have a private reason for doing or being involved in something. He has no political axe to grind. GO-TO GUY/GAL The person is frequently asked for help in that topic. Amanda’s our go-to gal for computer issues. MAKE A KILLING To earn a lot of money in a short time and with little effort. They made a killing with the sale of their London house.

Work-life balance I work for a global IT company, but because their headquarters is in the States, I do all my work online from home. That means that I don't waste time commuting or making idle chit-chat with colleagues. I work on a project basis, and this flexibility is very valuable to me because it means that I can easily take some time off when my children need me to go to their school performances, or if I need to make an appointment with the dentist. The downside is that without clear office hours, I tend to work well into the evening, sometimes without having dinner to finish a task. It can also get quite lonely working on my own, and I sometimes miss sharing ideas with colleagues. Adapted from https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/skills/reading/upper-intermediate-b2/work-life-balance

By the age of 20, Jake had already published his first book. Had + Past participle + before The boss had bitten everyone’s head off before I got with the answer. Before I got with the answer, the boss had bitten everyone’s head off. Had + Past participle + when Jazmin had already had a fit when HR solved the problem. When HR solved the problem, Jazmin had already had a fit. .There is another way to use past perfect using If clauses to talk about unreal situations in the past: If I had known, I would have told you. (Unit 45 will explain all about that). Past perfect can also be used in questions and negative sentences.

nextRows.title: To Consider 1. Past Perfect + By uses normally a noun phrase after the preposition. 2. Past Perfect + Before uses normally a clause in simple past after the preposition. 3. Past Perfect + When uses normally a clause in simple past after the preposition. 4. If we talk about one single event, there’s no need for us to use past perfect. Instead, we use simple past. E.G. Romans had spoken Latin. The correct form is: Romans spoke Latin. 5. We can use a past perfect clause alone when the context is already known. E.G. Context: A mum asked by phone if her son did his homework. -Totally, Mrs. Swan. Jax had already done his homework when you called.

sourceText: C. Read the following paragraph and extract sentences with the delexical verbs and tell your teacher what their intended meaning is.

What a day! Hi, have you ever had one of those days when everything seemed to go wrong? I'm sure you have, I know I have. I remember one particular day, I'd been invited to a party and there was someone going who I'd never met but I really wanted to meet, so I was quite excited about going to this party, and I maybe spent too long getting ready and I was a bit late when I was leaving the house, but not too late. But then I looked down and saw I had a hole in my tights! So I had to go back inside, change my tights, come out again, so I was getting a little bit late for the party, but not too bad. I got in my car, started driving, about halfway to the party my car stopped. I couldn't understand what was the matter until I looked at the petrol gauge: it had run out of petrol! Why? Because I'd lent my car to my son the day before and he'd used the petrol and he hadn't filled the car up! So I thought I'd ring the AA. I looked in my handbag to find my mobile phone, but I couldn't find it. Why? Because I'd left it next to my bed charging. So even though it was pouring with rain, I had to get out of my car, in my party clothes, walk to the petrol station and come back with petrol. By which time I was nearly 2 hours late. So, I was so flustered about being late, I started to drive and I just took a wrong turn and I ended up on this one-way system, totally lost, driving round and round for at least 45 minutes before I managed to get my bearings. So finally, I arrived at the party over 3 hours late and when I arrived the person I wanted to meet had just left, all the food had gone, and my host was horribly drunk. I was so disappointed that I just turned around and left and went back home. Have you ever had a terrible day like that, when everything went wrong? If you have, write and tell us about it. https://esol.britishcouncil.org/content/learners/grammar-and-vocabulary/grammar-lessons/one-those-days-past-perfect

Authored audio transcript:
Dylan, did you hear about Alex? No, Tanya, what happened? Ian told me that he said he was going to quit because he had a fight with the boss. What? They actually say that. Well, rumor has it, but how can we be sure? If we're not sure, we don't share that information. Let's not be noisy barkers. Come on, we're not gossiping, we're just shooting the breeze. You are right. Anyway, his things wouldn't be here if he had said he would quit. You're probably right. I'm going to call and ask him. Always looking for the front page, don't you girl? Yeah, you know me.

nextRows.title: IDIOM MEANING EXAMPLE SHOOT THE BREEZE To talk socially without exchanging too much information. Be careful! Just shoot the breeze. TO BE A NOSY PARKER To meddle in someone else’s business. Dean is such a nosy parker; always snooping around. A PORK PIE A story that is not true or that lacks of details. That guy always with his pork pies; we need a new janitor. TO SPIN THE YARN To divulge something that we are not certain to be true. I heard Mary left John, but I think our neighbors are just spinning the yarn. TO DISH THE DIRT To speak about others and reveal secrets or intimacies. There’s no good in dishing the dirt about others. TO GIVE THE GAME AWAY To reveal all we know about something. Don’t invite Jerry. He always gives the game away after a meeting. KEEP IT TO YOURSELF To not reveal information that is not yours even when you know it. Joe is proposing tonight, but keep it to yourself until then. MY LIPS ARE SEALED To keep a secret not sharing any information to others. Don’t worry, Annie; my lips are sealed

nextRows.title: We can use indirect speech for the following functions:

sourceText: We can use indirect speech for the following functions:

Functions Examples 1 Report what other people say They told us they had already finished the project. 2 Report questions other people make Jane asked Joe if he could buy dinner on his way home. 3 Report requests Carlos asked me to help him out.

To consider 1. When reporting requests, we normally use the verb ASK. Also, when doing it, we work with INFINITIVE FORMS as you see in the example. 2. Requests can be negative too. E.G. Please, don’t smoke here. -----> She asked me NOT to smoke here.

sourceText: C. Read the following paragraph and extract sentences with reported speech; what are they reporting? After that, read the text aloud to your teacher.

She said she loved me: A Case of a Crime of Passion. May 27th, 2021. After 35 years, the police department in our city has finally solved the mysterious death of the famous business woman Regina Mills. The chief of the department said that they had discovered a piece of evidence that had been overlooked years ago. That evidence directed them to Mrs. Mills’ husband, Frederick Thwan. Apparently, there was a note from the deceased that was not found until two weeks ago after her death anniversary where Mr. Smith, from the international bank, publicly told the press they had sustained an affair and claimed he had found a note from his lover saying, and we quote, He knows. Mr. Smith asked the police to reopen the case and he said that he would not stop until getting the responsible one. After 3 weeks or so of the reopening, the police linked the evidence to Mr. Thawn who confessed doing it and told the police he had done it because she said she loved him but it was not true. The case was finally closed and the police told the citizenry Mr. Thwn would never see the sun again. Roberts, J.

nextRows.title: PHRASES MEANING EXAMPLE A FUSS A display of unnecessary or excessive excitement, activity, or interest I don't know what all the fuss is about. A SCAM A deceptive scheme or trick used to cheat someone out of something, especially money The buying of the cars turned out to be just a scam. A STORM IN A TEACUP A small event that has been exaggerated out of proportion It was not that serious. Stop making a storm in a teacup. A CHARADE An absurd pretense intended to create a pleasant or respectable appearance I will ask Tina to cut the charade off. A LIP SERVICE An expression of agreement that is not supported by real conviction We cannot believe for a second the lip service given by the candidate. A SNOW JOB A deception or a fraud It is all a snow job, isn’t it? A SHARP PRACTICE A deceitful sneaky practice After the sharp practice was discovered the government has been keeping a closer eye on the private sector. A FISH TALE A lie or an exaggeration of the truth I don’t think he was telling the truth, it sounded like nothing but a good old fish tale to me.

nextRows.title: We can use tag questions for the following functions:

sourceText: We can use tag questions for the following functions:

Functions Examples 1 Check or confirm information You can’t swim, can you? They are not coming, are they? 2 Ask for agreement The food was delicious, wasn’t it? You love this movie, don’t you? 3 Wish to know the truth They were married, weren’t they? You have not told them, have you? 4. Express surprise or Interest You made this draft, did you? You had planned it all, had you?

To consider 1. If you pronounce the tag question with a rising intonation, the utterance will declare uncertainty. 2. If you pronounce the tag question with falling intonation, the utterance will declare certainty; you just need confirmation.

sourceText: C. Read the following paragraph and extract sentences with tag questions. What function are they representing. After that, read the text aloud to your teacher.

You know what it means, don’t you? It would be definitely amazing if we spoke at least three or four languages naturally, wouldn’t it? However, the reality is that most people are exposed to two languages or three as a top when being kids, which means that acquiring others would take time and dedication during life. Additionally, we all need to understand that learning a language requires a big effort, and that it will not come out of the blue will it? For instance, attending classes and looking for professional help are the first steps we have to take into account, but there is also the need for giving ourselves the chance to practice outside classes, opening spaces where we are in touch with the language and of course use what we learn. However, there are many who think that just attending lessons is enough, don’t they? Also, that there is no need to listen or to check what there was in my previous lesson in order to acquire a good level. Sadly, thinking like that only leads to self - frustration since those people learn the hard way that learning a language means so much more than coming to class, doesn’t it?

sourceText: Look at the phrases and discuss them with your teacher. Did you know them?

PHRASES MEANING EXAMPLE AT THE BACK OF YOUR MIND Something that you are not thinking about right now but is in your thoughts At the back of my mind is the fear of failing the exam. A BEE IN ONE’S BONNET An idea which constantly occupies your thoughts Eva's got a bee in her bonnet about moving to New York. LIVE / BE CLOUD CUCKOO It refers to an imaginary unrealistic place where everything is perfect and impossible things can happen I was living in cloud-cuckoo land about my marriage. A FLIGHT OF FANCY It means that something is very imaginative but not at all practical or sensible Jimmy often has good ideas but his latest proposal is just a flight of fancy! A LIGHT BULB MOMENT A sudden moment of inspiration, comprehension or realisation Harry had a light-bulb moment when he finally realised what was blocking the mechanism. BEAR/KEEP IN MIND To remember something Bear in mind that no food will be served on board. TOY WITH THE IDEA It means not to seriously think about something Sally has often toyed with the idea of moving abroad, but she's still here! BE ALL IN YOUR HEAD When something is just product of your imagination. It is not real. Don't be silly. Nobody is trying to harm you. It's all in your head!

nextRows.title: Structures ACTIVE VOICE PASSIVE VOICE Progressive Tenses The boys are painting the house. The house is being painted by the boys. She was preparing dinner for us. Dinner was being prepared for us. To Consider 1. In active voice, we focus on who /what does the action but in passive voice the focus goes on the object. 2. It is considered to be used in formal contexts; however, its use is very common. 3. In passive voice, the who / what makes the action can be omitted. 4. In perfect tenses, we need to add the word been before the participle. 5. The most common progressive tenses using passive voice are present and past. 6. When using present and past progressive, we use the verb to be + being + the participle. 7. Perfect progressive tenses may also work with passive voice; however, they are not very common. E.G. Our music has been annoying the man next door. → The man next door has been being annoyed by our music.

To Consider In active voice, we focus on who / what makes the action but in passive voice the focus goes on the object. It is considered to be used in formal contexts; however, its use is very common. In passive voice, the who / what makes the action can be omitted. In perfect tenses, we need to add the word been before the participle. The most common progressive tenses using passive voice are present and past. When using present and past progressive, we use the verb to be + being + the participle. Perfect progressive tenses may also work with passive voice; however, they are not very common. E.G. Our music has been annoying the man next door - The man next door has been being annoyed by our music.

sourceText: We can use passive voice for the following functions:

Functions Examples 1 State what things are made of The legs of the table are iron-made. The spoon was handcrafted in wood. 2 Declare when things are made / done The meeting will be set for tomorrow. Is this piano being played this week? 3 Point who things are made / done by The stuffed clams were made by Jake. Those dresses will be designed by Ericka. 4. Focus on objects rather than subjects in general actions Why was my burger eaten from the fridge? Five points will be taken from your test for cheating.
To consider Passive voice is not only used for the first three aspects; it can also be implemented in regular actions or everyday matters.

answerItems.rationale: The published item contains a one-letter subject error (The/They) and the non-idiomatic in the report. The original text and correction remain recorded so the published source is never overwritten.

John has done the house chores lately. The house chores have been done by John lately. Tim had borne in mind this idea for ages. This idea had been borne in mind by Tim for ages.

sourceText: C. Read the following paragraph and identify the sentences in passive voice. What function are they representing. After that, read the text aloud to your teacher.

Hong Kong on The Loop. The shipping industry says it's been hit by the global financial crisis and the recent spate of piracy attacks off Somalia. The chairman of the Hong Kong Ship Owners Association and chief executive of the Anglo-Eastern Group, Peter Cremers said ships are wary of sailing through the Gulf of Aden which has boosted costs as vessels are diverted. Analysts polled by Reuters news agency say they believe China's economy grew by just seven per cent in the last quarter of last year. If borne out by official data, this would be the worst figure in a decade. The Chinese authorities believe a minimum growth rate of eight per cent is needed to avoid severe unemployment and social disruption. China's manufacturing sector has been badly hit by recession in its main export markets. Temperatures over Hong Kong dipped on Sunday morning with the mercury plunging to minus one degree celsius in Ta Kwu Ling. A spokesman for the Observatory said it was the lowest temperature recorded in Ta Kwu Ling since a weather station was set up there, more than two decades ago. The Observatory says the average temperature recorded in the urban areas was 10 degrees. But, it was considerably colder in some parts of the New Territories. Adapted from https://www.eltbase.com/worksheet-714-news-stories

TWELFTH OF NEVER Something that will never come to pass If they had called Jane, this wouldn’t definitely have gone twelfth of the never. FEW AND FAR BETWEEN Events that are odd or rarely seen John calling? That is quite a few and far between. A COLD DAY IN HELL It means that something can’t be possible as hell going cold Hell would have gone on a cold day if Dinah had arrived on time. BEYOND BELIEF Something so great or terrible to be true That would've been beyond belief if they had prepared the play themselves. HUNKY DORY It may be understood as something out of this world or wicked The presentations was pretty hunky dory, congrats! A NO GO It means something is worthless or unreal It all would have been a no go if Mark had not stood up before the committee. OFF THE WALL When something is just strange or weird The new poster is just off the wall.

nextRows.title: We are able to express ideas about things that never came to happen in the past by using the third conditional. Check the chart.

sourceText: We are able to express ideas about things that never came to happen in the past by using the third conditional. Check the chart.

STRUCTURES STATEMENTS QUESTIONS Would Have + Past Participle + If clause. Joe would have come to his senses if she had been honest at first. Would Joe have come to his senses if she had been honest at first? The movie would not definitely have gone bad if they had kept the hunky dory story from the very beginning. Would the movie ever have gone bad? If clause + Would have + Past Participle If they had not gone off the wall, we would have probably closed that contract. What if they had not gone off the walls? If Jake had sought carefully, the investigation would have not turned out a failure. How would the investigation have turned out if Jake had sought carefully? To Consider 1. Would have is the auxiliary of this structure. 2. The if clause used here must go in past perfect. 3. Adverbs can be used here as they are used for other structures. 4. We need to use a comma when the if clause goes first. 5. We can use any interrogative words to make questions. 6. Indirect questions are possible as shown in the examples.

To Consider Would have is the auxiliary of this structure. The if clause used here must go in past perfect. Adverbs can be used here as they are used for other structures. data.transcript: So, how did the party go, Josh? Well, it would have gone better if it had hired Jill and her band to play. They didn't? What happened? I don't know, Neil. If I had known she was not going to be there, I would have never gone. Wow, I thought the contract was hers. I mean, I heard Tim saying they had agreed on having her play. I know. However, Dylan would have never approved that. They had something, and it went badly, so… Wow. Josh, I did not know, and since Dylan kind of has control over the club, they did not hire Jill. Just like that, man. No one would have never expected Dylan to do something like this. If they had had a good end, things may have not turned out in a no-go for Jill and her band. Too bad, man. I'm planning to call her, Neil. Would you join if she wants to go out? Of course. Count me in.

sourceText: C. Read the following paragraph and have a discussion with the teacher. After that, read the text aloud to your teacher.

The Sinking of Titanic. The sinking of the RMS Titanic was one of the worst maritime disasters in history. On April 14, 1912, at 11:40 p.m., the ‘unsinkable’ luxury ship hit an iceberg and sank in just under three hours with the loss of around 1500 lives. There are many different descriptions of the disaster by the surviving passengers and crew, but few people doubt that human error played a part in the tragedy. Let’s look at some of the things that went wrong. On the night of Sunday, 14 April 1912 the temperature was near freezing and the ocean was completely calm. Surviving 2nd Officer Charles Lightoller later wrote, "the sea was like glass". The ship’s course had been changed by the captain, but other than this, he saw no reason to slow down.The owner of the ship, Bruce Ismay, was also on board and had instructed the captain to speed up in order to break the record for a transatlantic voyage. The captain agreed, but perhaps if he had known of the messages the ship had received in the radio room, he would have acted differently. According to a ship ahead called the Mesaba, lots of large icebergs were in the area. These messages did not reach him. There were three teams of lookouts on board keeping constant watch for obstacles in the ship’s path, but as Charles Lightoller said at the British inquiry, "Everything was against us, there was no moon, no wind, no binoculars and with the dark side of the iceberg facing the ship, the lookouts were powerless.”

sourceText: When the alarm was finally raised the crew acted very quickly but it was already too late to save the ship. Within twenty minutes of the collision the ship had flooded, so the captain ordered the lifeboats to be prepared, filled with women and children, and lowered into the water. This didn’t go well, regulations about the number of lifeboats a ship should carry were already out of date when the Titanic set sail, and even if the evacuation had been better organised, there wouldn’t have been enough boats to hold everybody. Meanwhile, the crew were sending out distress signals. The first message was "sinking, need immediate assistance," and then "SOS". Several ships responded, including the Mount Temple, Frankfurt, and the Titanic's sister ship, Olympic, but they were too far away. The closest ship to respond was the Carpathia, which arrived in about four hours, too late to save everybody. Various distress flares launched from the sinking ship were also ineffective, including those seen by a ship called the Californian, whose captain, Stanley Lord, had ordered his crew to stop the ship for the night because of the icebergs. When Captain Lord was informed of the flares he failed to respond because he did not think they were important. Nor did the crew of the Californian wake their radio operator, who had gone to bed for the night. And what of Bruce Ismay, who many believe acted without regard for safety by requiring an unprepared ship to sail at such speed in spite of the danger? History tells us that he survived, but from the lifeboat turned his back on his beautiful ship as it sank That night, of a total of 2,208 people, only 712 were rescued by the Carpathia, while 1,496 perished. If the lifeboats had been filled to capacity, 1,178 people could have been saved. If there had been enough lifeboats, maybe everybody could have been saved. However, we may never know for sure. Article adapted from https://esol.britishcouncil.org/sites/default/files/attachments/informational-page/The_Sinking_of_the_Third_Condition.pdf

Come on Nolan. nextRows.title: PHRASES MEANING EXAMPLE A SMOKING GUN Something that is obvious; an indisputable truth You should have seen the smoking gun; that man could not be trusted. HIDDEN AGENDA Something that may refer to a secret plan or an implication I would not have expected Freddy to have a hidden agenda. A SHOT IN THE DARK To have an ide or suspicion about someone or something Thank God I had already gotten a shot in the dark about Tim, he almost got away with that. NUTS AND BOLTS The detailed information about someone or something and how it works If it had been me, I would have gone nut and bolts with Jenny; now she’s gone! AN INSIDE STORY Considered as an advice or a hot tip What an inside story John has just dropped us. A STRAW IN THE WIND It refers to an indication or sign that one can see or get from someone or something We should have seen the straw in the wind; now, we can’t do anything. UPPER HAND It means someone or something has a position of advantage and control Fortunately, I had already upper-handed the rest of the contestants. TIP OF THE ICEBERG The small piece or amount of something that we can see Handing over the project was just the tip of the iceberg.

sourceText: We are able to express opinions, suggestions and expectations in the past by using the following structures. Check the chart.

STRUCTURES STATEMENTS QUESTIONS Should Have + Past Participle Dylan should have called them before going. What should he have done before going? If it had been me, I should have brought more money. What should you have done? Would have + Past Participle My family would have wanted him to be different, but he wasn’t. How would have your family wanted him to be? He would not have expected me to drop school. Would he have expected you to drop school? Must have + Past Participle We must have seen the straw in the wind, but we did not. Would you have seen the straw in the wind? If he had not done things that way , the boss must have given him the chance. What if he had not done things that way?

data.transcript: Sometimes it is so hard to let go, you know? Bad things happen and when you look back, you said to yourself that you should have acted differently. Not all the time things go the way we want, in fact, there is a great chance they turn out to be completely different as we would have wanted them to be. Sometimes, I even think that I must not have said something the way I did, but one cannot cry over spilled milk. These kinds of situations help us realize that there is more to be assessed and internalized about our lives and the way we live them. I know this is something we would have never admitted if we had not lived enough. Don't you agree?

Not all the time things go the way we want, in fact, there is a great chance they turn out to be completely different as we would have wanted them to be. Sometimes, I even think that I must not have said something the way I did, but one cannot cry over spilled milk. These kinds of situations help us realize that there is more to be assessed and internalized about our lives and the way we live them. I know this is something we would have never admitted if we had not lived enough. Don't you agree?
