sourceText: C. Read the following paragraph and have a discussion with the teacher. After that, read the text aloud to your teacher.

'Friends' cast sings show's theme song with James Corden James Corden, host of the reunion that we all couldn't stop talking about, recruited the cast of "Friends" for a special segment that aired on his show Wednesday night. In the clip, Corden helps transport the cast -- Jennifer Aniston, Courteney Cox, Lisa Kudrow, Matt LeBlanc, Matthew Perry and David Schwimmer -- to the set and uses the brief ride through the Warner Bros. lot, where they used to film, to channel "Carpool Karaoke." Do you really need to ask the song choice? We all would have chosen the same, wouldn’t we? After belting The Rembrandt's "I'll Be There For You," Corden and the cast get cozy in Central Perk for some fun and games, that turns some on the couches to tears as we all must’ve expected. "Friends: The Reunion" was released last month on HBO Max. (CNN, like HBO, is owned by Warner Media.) and it was said to be the last episode (reunion) of the cast despite fans would have desired it to be one of many to come. While the streamer has not released viewing numbers, Variety reported that the highly-anticipated special may have performed nearly as well as "Wonder Woman 1984," the sequel to the 2017 blockbuster superhero film. Nevertheless, it is a fact that thousands if not millions of people watched the reunion and we would not have expected less from a TV show that is clearly part of pop culture and an iconic program for masses. Article adapted from https://edition.cnn.com/2021/06/17/entertainment/friends-james-corden/index.html

sourceText: We are able to express regrets in different ways. Check the chart.

STRUCTURES STATEMENTS QUESTIONS N + Should Have + Past Participle I should have told them the truth before, What should you have done before? I shouldn’t have said those things. What should you have said? If only + N + Had + Past Participle If only she had acted differently, the story would be different. How would this have ended up if she had acted differently? If only I had expected nothing from them. I certainly look like an idiot now. Would you really have expected nothing from them? N + regret + V (ing) I regret calling her and letting her know about this. What do you regret? They did not regret making a scandal in front of everyone. Where they even sorry about that?

sourceText: We can use these structures to state the following functions:

Functions Examples 1 Express life regrets I should have bought the car; now, I’m stuck here. 2 Lament on something If only they had listened to their parents, but they didn’t. 3. Regret one’s doings I regret inviting them so badly; they ruined our christmas party.

To consider We can also use - wish - to talk about things we want / wanted to be different. Present: I wish you did not live so far away. / I wish he’d stop talking. Past: They wish they hadn’t drunk so much. Now they are sick.

I wish you didn't do as I did and that the outcomes of your decisions come at their best.

Regret can Seriously Damage your Mental Health There was once a banker in his 50s who had worked seven days a week for 25 years and become a very wealthy man. Then, at the apex of his career, he looked around him and realised that he had entirely neglected his family; as a result, his family had rejected him. The regret was overwhelming, and came out in panic attacks every Sunday. Would this man be able to find a way out of this cruel place he had created for himself? This man was a patient of the psychoanalyst David Morgan, of the Institute of Psychoanalysis, who spent several years helping him explore what had compelled him to work so hard and to ignore his children (he has been anonymised and gave Morgan permission to use his case). It became clear that this need to become richer than everyone else had roots in his very early childhood, when he watched his parents nearly starve to death during the 1980s miners’ strike. He had, unconsciously, repeated this by impoverishing his children by not being there for them, in turn impoverishing himself of these loving relationships, in his efforts to overcome the traumatic poverty of his childhood. “That complicated understanding,” Morgan explains, “freed things up, setting his regret in a generational context so he didn’t have to feel quite so guilty for acting something out, because it was beyond his ken. It doesn’t mean that he can’t feel real pain, but that pain is given a sense of history.” This meant his regret could be understood and given meaning – and that changed his life.

sourceText: Regret can be all-consuming, and it can destroy lives. We can see it all around us, whether it is the man who cannot forgive himself for cheating on his first girlfriend and has not had a serious relationship in 30 years. Or the woman who is so tied up in wishing she’d had a child with her ex-partner, instead of breaking up with him, that she cannot find happiness in her current circumstances. It is not unusual for patients to seek therapy because they feel plagued by regret and unable to live full lives because of it, says Morgan, whether it is over affairs, career choices or relationships. The kind of regret that brings people to his consulting room is “paranoid and persecutory. It’s: ‘Oh God, I’m so terrible, I’m dreadful,’” he says. It is self-flagellation, and it can be incredibly damaging to our mental health. It is exhausting, it sucks all joy and fulfilment from our days and it leaves us stuck, always looking backwards and unable to move forward in our lives. The cognitive behaviour therapist Windy Dryden says that, when we are trapped in this cycle of regret, characterised by rigidity and inflexibility, we only seem able to blame ourselves for what has happened, rather than seeing our behaviour in a wider context and understanding why we took the path we did based on the information we had at the time. Under these conditions, regret will become toxic. Keep reading the article here: https://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2019/jun/27/regret-can-seriously-damage-your-mental-health-heres-how-to-leave-it-behind

data.transcript: Have you ever wondered how you could have turned out if you had had a different family or been raised differently? I do it all the time, in fact, I always wonder what I might have been like if I had come from a rich family. I guess we all wonder about things we don't have or things we are not. However, I certainly consider that one must not hold his breath on things that may not occur anytime soon or at all. Nevertheless, once in a blue moon, you might get lucky, so who knows. Maybe, fantasizing about being rich is not that bad. If you asked me, I think I may have ended up helping people if I had all the money in the world, for sure, I would have loved to get the same parents I did since they might have given me the same values they gave me even if they were wealthy people.

Authored audio transcript:
Have you ever wondered how you could have turned out if you had had a different family or been raised differently? I do it all the time, in fact, I always wonder what I might have been like if I had come from a rich family. I guess we all wonder about things we don't have or things we are not. However, I certainly consider that one must not hold his breath on things that may not occur anytime soon or at all. Nevertheless, once in a blue moon, you might get lucky, so who knows. Maybe, fantasizing about being rich is not that bad. If you asked me, I think I may have ended up helping people if I had all the money in the world, for sure, I would have loved to get the same parents I did since they might have given me the same values they gave me even if they were wealthy people.

nextRows.title: PHRASES MEANING EXAMPLE WHEN PIGS FLY To be sure something will never happen You’ll get that once pigs fly. ONCE IN A BLUE MOON A very rare event to happen John gets straight as once in a blue moon. HELL FREEZES Something impossible to occur They could have gotten the offer if hell had frozen. FEW AND FAR BETWEEN To indicate rarely seen events Just in a few and far between, he might have obtained the score. NOT TO HOLD SOMEONE’S BREATH Expresses something people hope for will likely never happen He should not have held his breath on that. TO GET BLOOD FROM A STONE Generally taken to mean a pointless task due to its difficulty Don’t you try get blood from that stone; she will never like you. TWELFTH OF NEVER Something that will happen on the "Twelfth of Never" will never come to pass She could have answered yes in the twelfth of never. TIBB’S EVE To refer to something that does not / did not / will not exist We’re coming back on Tibb’s eve.

nextRows.title: STRUCTURES STATEMENTS QUESTIONS Could + Have + Past Participle I could have gotten lost if we had not seen then on time. What could have happened to them? You could have said that before all went to nothing. What could I have said? May + Have + Past Participle John may have caught that flu at the hospital. Where may John have caught that flu? Did you eat a burger even being a vegetarian? They might have been here, but they are gone now. Were they here before?

sourceText: We can use these structures to state the following functions:

Functions Examples 1 Express probabilities in the past They might have ended up together, but Shane ruined it. 2 Make guesses about past events They could have gotten lost since they did not arrive last night. 3. State impossible past events If Kyle was at work, he could have not committed the murder

To consider 1. We can use all possibility modals for functions 1 and 2. 2. Function 2 needs a logic complement to make it look like a guess not as a possibility. 3. Function number three works with could + have only. 4. You may see function 3 also working with can’t + have.

What if Dinosaurs had survived? Around 66 million years ago, a 14 km-wide asteroid smashed into our planet. An estimated 15 billion tonnes of soot spread through the atmosphere, creating one long night that lasted several years and made photosynthesis all but impossible. It heralded an endless winter that saw average temperatures fall by as much as 28oC. These are the conditions that the few wretched creatures that survived the initial impact had to endure – not to mention the earthquakes, tsunamis, wildfires and volcanic eruptions that swiftly followed in its wake. Around three-quarters of all species went extinct and no animal bigger than a Labrador dog survived. But according to researchers at the University of Texas, things could have been very different. They reported findings that had the asteroid struck Earth just a few minutes earlier, it would have hit the deep ocean rather than the shallow sea of the Yucatan Peninsula in present-day Mexico. Had that been the case, then the damage would have been more localised. Some of the dinosaurs far from the impact site might have survived, and the world would be a different place today. In our own history, only the feathered theropod dinosaurs (a group of bipedal dinosaurs) we know as birds made it through the calamity, but how would things have turned out if their larger relatives had joined them? Would dinosaurs still be alive today and could mammals such as humans have evolved? What would our world look like if we shared it with the descendants of animals like T. rex and Triceratops?

sourceText: “I’m sure a fairly nice diversity of non-avian dinosaurs would still be here,” says Dr Stephen Brusatte, a palaeontology at the University of Edinburgh. “If there was no sudden, catastrophic shock of the asteroid, I really don’t see anything that’s happened since – whether it was the spread of grasslands; changing ocean currents; the separation of Antarctica from South America, which caused a cold snap; or the more recent Ice Ages – that would have knocked off the dinosaurs.” Over the years many have tried to imagine what kind of creatures dinosaurs might have evolved into had they survived. The most famous attempt is a 1988 book called The New Dinosaurs: An Alternative Evolution, by Scottish geologist and author Dougal Dixon. For this magnificent work of speculative zoology, Dixon conjured up creatures such as the ‘cutlasstooth’ – a pack-hunting, sabre-toothed predator from South America; the ‘cribrum’ – a flamingo-like, filter-feeding theropod from Australia; and the ‘gourmand’ – a relative of T. rex that lost its front limbs entirely and developed a distensible jaw to allow it to rapidly swallow prey whole, much like a snake. Perhaps this last idea isn’t entirely wide of the mark. Dr Tom Holtz, an expert on theropod dinosaurs at the University of Maryland in the US, says that both tyrannosaurs and abelisaurs, the two types of big meat-eater present in the Late Cretaceous, are notable for their tiny forelimbs. “Given that arms were non-critical for hunting, it’s possible that a Cenozoic [current geological era] tyrannosaur could have been armless,” says Holtz. The beginning of the Cenozoic Era (which spans the period from 66 million years ago until the present day) might essentially have been an ecological extension of the Late Cretaceous. GRASP AT A STRAW To be unsure about something and still state an opinion I think he is just grasping at a straw. READ SOMEONE’S MIND To deduce what someone else is thinking She will never call; It’s like I read her mind. A SHOT IN THE DARK To venture guessing something you are not certain about John accused Oliver, he just took a shot in the dark. ANYONE’S GUESS A mystery or something unpredictable It's anyone's guess what his next book will be about. TAKE A STAB AT To give it a try or a shot Mary went for it and took a stab at the application. SEAT-OF-THE-PANTS To describe something improvised or done based on prior experience Why are you doing this by seat-of-the-pants? BARK UP THE WRONG TREE To be wrong about something or someone; To be wrong about the reasons or ways to achieve something Stop accusing me lady, you’re barking up the wrong tree,

sourceText: C. Read the following paragraph and have a discussion with the teacher. After that, read aloud the text to your teacher.

Possible Potential Outcomes from COVID-19 Complications on Testes: Lesson from SARS Infection Coronavirus infection disease-2019 (COVID-19) gained worldwide fame after deadly outbreak in China and its subsequent spread to many countries. So far, COVID-19 is not fully contained, and new cases are arising on daily bases in various countries, Imagine if it keeps growing. Due to zoonotic nature and human-to-human spread, COVID-19 is considered pandemic with more causalities in developing countries. Full genome analysis revealed its resemblance with severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS) virus with minor variation in non-structural proteins. Both viruses use the common angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE2) receptor to attach to the epithelial cells of the target organs. Currently, in case someone gets COVID-19, those patients are treated with drugs that are used for lungs infections. However, ACE2 has high expression in other human organs such as kidney and testes. So what if that’s not enough? Thus, it is assumed that, like SARS, it may have adverse effects on other vital organs, which have dominant expression of ACE2. In testis, SARS affected patients displayed peritubular fibrosis, extensive germ cell disruption, damage of blood-testis barrier integrity and more frequent occurrence of apoptosis. Here, we critically discuss the possible adverse effects of COVID-19 on the testes of patients along with future precautions to overcome the complications of reproductive organs. Adapted from: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33115584/

Possible Potential Outcomes from COVID-19 Complications on Testes: Lesson from SARS Infection Coronavirus infection disease-2019 (COVID-19) gained worldwide fame after deadly outbreak in China and its subsequent spread to many countries. So far, COVID-19 is not fully contained, and new cases are arising on daily bases in various countries, Imagine if it keeps growing. Due to zoonotic nature and human-to-human spread, COVID-19 is considered pandemic with more causalities in developing countries. Full genome analysis revealed its resemblance with severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS) virus with minor variation in non-structural proteins. Both viruses use the common angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE2) receptor to attach to the epithelial cells of the target organs. Currently, in case someone gets COVID-19, those patients are treated with drugs that are used for lungs infections. However, ACE2 has high expression in other human organs such as kidney and testes. So what if that’s not enough? Thus, it is assumed that, like SARS, it may have adverse effects on other vital organs, which have dominant expression of ACE2. In testis, SARS affected patients displayed peritubular fibrosis, extensive germ cell disruption, damage of blood-testis barrier integrity and more frequent occurrence of apoptosis. Here, we critically discuss the possible adverse effects of COVID-19 on the testes of patients along with future precautions to overcome the complications of reproductive organs. Adapted from: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33115584/

data.transcript: Hey Carl, imagine you had the chance to be part of an important national organization. How cool would that be? Don't even mention it, Taylor. If only I could get there once I finished college, knocking on the wood now. You have to go for that brass ring, but it's kind of difficult, right? Totally, man. Sometimes I even think I am in a false paradise when I think about that. Yeah, what if people there knew you? That would make the whole difference. If only I could get an opportunity. I guess dreaming is free. Come on, I have seen regular people like us getting to higher places. So do not be discouraged, Carl. I wish I always saw the bright side as you normally do. nextRows.title: PHRASES MEANING EXAMPLE FEEL THE PINCH To experience hardship, especially financial. Staff, we’re beginning to feel the pinch as the dispute entered its third week. SEE THE FIT To consider it correct or acceptable to do something. Why did the company see fit to give you the job? KNOCK ON WOOD said after a confident or positive statement, to express a hope for one's good luck to continue. I haven't been banned yet, knock on wood. FIRE IN THE BELLY A powerful sense of ambition or determination. He lacks the fire in his belly necessary to seek the presidency. HOPE AGAINST HOPE Hope or wish for with little reason or justification. I'm hoping against hope that someone will return my wallet. FOOL’S PARADISE A state of happiness based on a person's not knowing about or denying the existence of potential trouble. They were living in a fool's paradise, refusing to accept that they were in debt. BRASS RING A very desirable prize, goal, or opportunity He made his first try for the brass ring when he ran for mayor a few years ago. GAME PLAN A strategy worked out in advance, especially in sports, politics, or business. If he has a game plan for winning the deal, only he understands it.

sourceText: We are able to express ideas about things or events not likely to happen through the use of different expressions and regular grammar.

PHRASES EXAMPLES What if… What if Jane came tonight to the party? Just picture how awkward it would be. Imagine that / if… Imagine you fell in front of your classmates; would you laugh at yourself? If only… If only you could come home these days. / If only I had more time, but I am always busy. I wish… I wish we didn’t feel the pinch but there’s nothing we could do. / I wish it could be different. To Consider 1. We work with these phrases using the simple past tense. 2. When using what if we have to close the sentence with a question mark. 3. Could and would play a major role.

data.transcript: I wish we all could see things differently. If only we had more perspective and were more responsible, socially speaking, the world may not have gone through so many rough times as it has so far. What if we thought things thoroughly? We could act better instead of just acting. What if world leaders did put their people first? We would be in a better place as nations, even going further than others had gone before. We have to understand that wishing is not enough, moving forward needs to go for a game plan in order to get the brass ring we all expect. If only we did not hope for the best, but made something about it, the world would turn into a better place.

sourceText: C. Read the following paragraph and have a discussion with the teacher. After that, read the text aloud to your teacher. Check the full article in the link below.

Achieving Your Wishes : Will Wishing Work? Do you wish you had a better job, bigger house, more friends, better health, less worries, and greater happiness? We all engage in wishing, but should we? Should we wish for more or be satisfied with what we have? Why can't we do both? Just because we are satisfied with what we have doesn't mean we can't or shouldn't wish for more. After all, isn't self-improvement or personal-development about wishing for more? No, there isn't anything wrong with wishing. A wish is merely the voice of our Higher Self reminding us that we have boundless potential and urging us to take advantage of it. If anything, we should wish to have, be, and do more because that's how we help to create a better world; if only we always thought that way.. It is only when we have more than we need that we can share what we have with those who have less than they need. It is only when we are healthy that we can help the sick. And it is only when we are strong that we can help the weak. As you can see, wishing plays an important role, for we either allow ourselves to become what others will make of us, or we wish to become something better. Did you ever toss a coin into a wishing well and make a wish? What if you had your own wishing well? Aware of it or not, that's precisely what we have. We have a personal genie within us. It is our subconscious. Its sole purpose is to serve us. It serves us by regulating our heart and breathing rate, body temperature, and the flow of hormones, just to name a few of its many functions. But another major function of the subconscious is to grant our every wish! And it works tirelessly, 24/7, granting us what it believes we want. Adapted from: https://www.rotaryeclubone.org/makeups/articles/achievingyourwishe/

After all, isn't self-improvement or personal-development about wishing for more? No, there isn't anything wrong with wishing. A wish is merely the voice of our Higher Self reminding us that we have boundless potential and urging us to take advantage of it. If anything, we should wish to have, be, and do more because that's how we help to create a better world; if only we always thought that way.. It is only when we have more than we need that we can share what we have with those who have less than they need. It is only when we are healthy that we can help the sick. And it is only when we are strong that we can help the weak. As you can see, wishing plays an important role, for we either allow ourselves to become what others will make of us, or we wish to become something better. Did you ever toss a coin into a wishing well and make a wish? What if you had your own wishing well? Aware of it or not, that's precisely what we have. We have a personal genie within us. It is our subconscious. Its sole purpose is to serve us. It serves us by regulating our heart and breathing rate, body temperature, and the flow of hormones, just to name a few of its many functions. But another major function of the subconscious is to grant our every wish! And it works tirelessly, 24/7, granting us what it believes we want. nextRows.title: PHRASES MEANING EXAMPLE CASTLES IN THE AIR To have big dreams about an idea or project that may not come true. What if all this had been just castles in the air? CLASS ACT A person or thing displaying impressive and stylish excellence. The writing and the look of the magazine make it a real class act. HUNKY DORY Expression used to say all is going well. Everything is hunky-dory. QUEER AS A THREE-DOLLAR BILL Completely and obviously false or fake; not genuine or authentic in the slightest.. The guy claims to teach you how to get rich in a hurry, but the whole thing sounds as queer as a three-dollar bill. LARGER THAN LIFE To attract special attention because of unusual and flamboyant appearance or behavior or seem disproportionately important. Your problems seem larger than life at that time of the night. OFF THE MARK When something or someone is incorrect or inaccurate. The accusation was a little wide of the mark. OFF BASE To be mistaken. Your argument is so off base. OFF THE WALL To be eccentric or unconventional. Some other times to be really angry. The president was off the wall about the article.

nextRows.title: We are able to express ideas about things or event that did not happen through the use of different expressions and regular grammar.

sourceText: We are able to express ideas about things or event that did not happen through the use of different expressions and regular grammar.

PHRASES EXAMPLES What if… What if Charles had taken Mary to the party? He would have loosened there! Imagine that / if… Imagine you hadn’t called Joe’s parents; When would have they known? Suppose / Supposing that Supposing we had not gone to the doctor, we could have gotten worse. I wish… I wish I had called her; now, I will never know if she felt the same for me. To Consider 1. We work with these phrases using the past perfect tense. 2. When using what if we have to close the sentence with a question mark. 3. Could and would play a major role. Especially for complementing the sentences. 4. Some other modals may be useful depending on the context.

data.transcript: I wish I had had the chances youngsters get nowadays. Imagine if we had been able to see the wonders they see now through the Internet and the mass media, we could have gotten a different perspective of life, well, probably. Though, we did pretty hunky-dory, in our times, I must say. If we had had the tech kids have now, things may have ended up a little different. I truly think every generation gets what it needs and that comes with pros and cons. When we had gotten mobiles back then, we might have missed the great childhood we had, so after all, I guess we did not have such a boring childhood, even when not having what kids have now.

sourceText: C. Read the following paragraph and have a discussion with the teacher. After that, read the text aloud to your teacher. Check the full article in the link below.

Global Disasters that never Came to happen: The Impending Ice Age An April 28, 1975 article in Newsweek Magazine titled "The Cooling World" warned that the world could freeze over before we knew it. A year earlier, Time ran an article titled, "A New Ice Age?" The media of the mid-70's latched onto the idea of impending icy death, imagine if it had become true. But where did this come from? Between 1945 and the 1970's global temperatures had decreased. Scientists have since figured out that sulphate aerosols caused cooling, by blocking and reflecting sunlight as well as serving as seeds for cloud coverage. At the same time scientific papers explaining about how the earth's orbital patterns affect global weather and the creation of ice ages were being published. The media seemed to pick up geologist saying an ice age could be soon — but not really understanding that thousands of years is "soon" to a geologist; but what if that had happened? We would not probable have written this article. Despite the media hype, the scientific journals were either unsure about how humans were affecting the climate, or already predicting the possibility of global warming due to CO2. Current research shows the high level of CO2 in the atmosphere is preventing any growth of the ice sheets. The Ice Age fear has come back recently, most likely because of the 2012 hysteria, but this time in conjunction with the sun's solar cycles. Bad Astronomy explains why you don't need invest in parkas quite yet. Incidentally, Newsweek issued a correction to the 1975 article in 2006, since by then it was clear an Ice Age hadn't wiped us all out. If only people had been more cautious in the information they linked, we (new generations) may have turned more eager for facts than farandula. Adapted from: https://gizmodo.com/9-global-disasters-that-never-came-to-pass-5943220

nextRows.title: We are able to express ideas about things or events yet to happen through two main grammar structures.

sourceText: We are able to express ideas about things or events yet to happen through two main grammar structures.

FUTURE PERFECT FUTURE CONTINUOUS The guests are coming at 8PM. I’ll have finished cooking by then. In two years’ time, I’ll have had my kids, so I’ll be a parent. Will the kids have gone to bed when I get back? When you get out of the office tomorrow, I’ll be boarding a plane. Come on July, I won’t be working then. Will you be starting work earlier with your new job? To Consider 1. Future perfect works with Will + Have + Past participle. 2. It uses time phrases like: By then, In some years’ time, when clauses, by the time, etc. 3. Future continuous works with To be + V(ing). 4. The time phrases for future continuous may be shared with future perfect; though, the ones used here are more specific as seen in the examples. 5. Both can add Wh words to make questions.

The expert guide to space colonies With our rising planet’s population competing for space and resources, some people are convinced we need to look beyond Earth to help ensure humanity’s survival; What will we have had when that time comes?. As Elon Musk, the entrepreneur behind space tourism company SpaceX put it recently: “I think there is a strong argument for making life multiplanetary in order to safeguard the existence of humanity in the event that something catastrophic were to happen.” Even if you don’t believe this bleak vision, it’s hard to ignore the eternal human instinct to discover the undiscovered – an urge that could push people beyond the safety of our planet, and we reckon we will be doing something about it when time comes. And there might not be as many hurdles as you might think. “We are at the level of technology where we can imagine leaving the planet for a few nearby places in our Solar System,” former astronaut Jeffrey Hoffman, who will present his ideas at our summit, told BBC Future previously. “The Moon is just around the corner, and Mars isn’t that far away. We have the possibility of at least making the first steps of those voyages in our own lifetimes.” What could a space colony look like? One possible idea goes as far back as the 1920s. Austro-Hungarian rocket pioneer Herman Potočnik imagined a circular spacecraft - rather like a flying saucer – that rotates to create artificial gravity while a large, concave mirror could focus sunlight for an energy source. As far-fetched as this may sound, the idea has lingered over the years – most notably in the mid-1970s by the late Princeton physicist Gerard O’Neill, and again by the space think tank British Interplanetary Society. Before you dismiss the idea of floating colonies completely, it’s worth noting that the British Interplanetary Society predicted we would reach the Moon three decades before it actually happened, so imagine where it will have gotten once it sets its mind on it. Adapted from: https://www.bbc.com/future/article/20141002-time-to-plan-a-space-colony
